chunks: And in the narration of al-Sakuni, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, he said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام, when the childbirth of a woman was at hand, would say: 'Remove whoever of the women is in the house, so that a woman is not the first to look at his private parts.'
ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about modesty and who should be present during childbirth?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a practice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام during childbirth, instructing that the women be removed from the house so that a woman would not be the first to look at the newborn boy's private parts. It reflects a concern for modesty and etiquette surrounding birth and bodily privacy in the family setting.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4925 - In the narration of Al-Sakuni from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), he said:

"When Imam Ali ibn Al-Hussain (as) was present at the time of a woman's childbirth, he would say:
'Remove all the women from the house so that a woman is not the first to look at the child's private parts.'"
